adjudication.rationale: The diff adds documentation warnings in `docs/guides/operator/advanced-configuration.adoc` stating the Operator "will fail" if `rolling-updates` is not enabled, but the only concrete enforcement added in this PR is in the CLI commands (`UpdateCompatibilityCheck`/`UpdateCompatibilityMetadata`) via `Profile.isFeatureEnabled(Profile.Feature.ROLLING_UPDATES)` and exiting with `CompatibilityResult.FEATURE_DISABLED`. adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces `CompatibilityResult.FEATURE_DISABLED = 4` and both `UpdateCompatibilityCheck` and `UpdateCompatibilityMetadata` exit with 4 when `Profile.Feature.ROLLING_UPDATES` is not enabled (i.e., a precondition failure before running the compatibility logic). In `docs/guides/server/update-compatibility.adoc`, the new exit-code row for 4 is phrased under the same “Rolling Upgrade is not possible” framing as actual compatibility outcomes, which can conflate a configuration/precondition error with a compatibility verdict for automation/pipeline consumers, and it also applies to `metadata` per the code.

adjudication_records.issue_text: quarkus/tests/integration/src/test/java/org/keycloak/it/cli/dist/UpdateCommandDistTest.java:48 — The renumbered exit-code contract is untested: testFeatureNotEnabled does not assert exit code 4 and testWrongVersions does not assert exit code 3

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes the exit-code contract in `CompatibilityResult` (`RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE` from 4 to 3, and adds `FEATURE_DISABLED = 4`). In `UpdateCommandDistTest`, the new `testFeatureNotEnabled` only asserts the error message and does not assert the expected exit code (4). Likewise, `testWrongVersions` asserts error output but does not assert the recreate/compatibility failure exit code (now 3). This is a specific, diff-grounded gap in test coverage of the renumbered exit codes rather than a demonstrated functional defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: docs/guides/operator/advanced-configuration.adoc:446 — Operator docs require only `spec.features.enabled: rolling-updates`, but the PR itself had to rebuild the custom image with `--features=rolling-updates` (build-time option), so users of optimized custom images are not told they must rebuild

adjudication.rationale: The operator docs change only shows enabling `rolling-updates` via the CR (`spec.features.enabled`). However, the diff also updates `operator/scripts/Dockerfile-custom-image` to add `--features=rolling-updates` to `kc.sh build`, implying custom/optimized images built via this script must enable the feature at build time as well. The operator documentation snippet at `docs/guides/operator/advanced-configuration.adoc` does not mention this extra requirement for users building optimized custom images, so the finding is a valid, diff-grounded documentation completeness issue rather than a functional bug in code.

adjudication_records.issue_text: docs/guides/operator/advanced-configuration.adoc:448 — Docs promise the Operator "will fail" when update.strategy is set without the feature, but no operator-side validation/status condition is added in this change, so behavior is undefined/silent for CR users

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds docs in `advanced-configuration.adoc` stating the Operator will fail unless the preview feature `rolling-updates` is enabled, but the shown code changes do not add any Operator-side reconciliation/validation or status condition to enforce or surface this requirement. The only enforcement added in this diff is on the CLI side (`UpdateCompatibilityCheck/Metadata` exit early if `Profile.Feature.ROLLING_UPDATES` is disabled) plus tests/docs/Dockerfile adjustments. Whether the Operator truly "will fail" without the feature cannot be verified from this diff, but the finding’s point about missing Operator-side validation/status signaling is grounded in what’s changed here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: docs/guides/templates/kc.adoc:53 — Macro appends a hard-coded `--features=rolling-updates` that overrides any user-supplied `--features`/KC_FEATURES, contradicting the guide's instruction to pass the exact same configuration to metadata/check

The diff does not show how `${parameters}` is constructed in all usages, does not show any guide text about “exact same configuration,” and does not establish option-precedence/override behavior if multiple `--features` are provided or if `KC_FEATURES` is set.

adjudication_records.issue_text: docs/guides/operator/advanced-configuration.adoc:446 — Docs state the Operator "will fail" without `rolling-updates`, but no operator code in this change checks or gates on the feature, so the documented behavior isn't implemented (and the example makes it look required even for `Recreate`)

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a docs CAUTION in `docs/guides/operator/advanced-configuration.adoc` stating the Operator "will fail" unless `rolling-updates` is enabled, but the only concrete gating added in this PR is for the *CLI* commands (`UpdateCompatibilityCheck`/`UpdateCompatibilityMetadata` check `Profile.isFeatureEnabled(Profile.Feature.ROLLING_UPDATES)` and exit with `CompatibilityResult.FEATURE_DISABLED`). In the operator-related code shown, there is no controller/reconciler logic that checks/enforces the feature; only tests/docs/examples were updated to enable it (`UpgradeTest` sets `FeatureSpec.enabledFeatures`, Dockerfile adds `--features=rolling-updates`). This makes the documentation claim look stronger/more general than what is implemented in the shown operator code, and the example implies it’s required even when `strategy: Recreate`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: quarkus/tests/integration/src/test/java/org/keycloak/it/cli/dist/UpdateCommandDistTest.java:48 — testFeatureNotEnabled only asserts the message and never the new FEATURE_DISABLED=4 exit code (or RECREATE=3 anywhere), so the renumbered exit-code sentinels have no test coverage

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces new/renumbered exit codes in `CompatibilityResult` (`RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE` changed to 3 and new `FEATURE_DISABLED = 4`) and the CLI commands now explicitly call `picocli.exit(CompatibilityResult.FEATURE_DISABLED)` when `rolling-updates` is not enabled (`UpdateCompatibilityCheck.run()` / `UpdateCompatibilityMetadata.run()`). However, `UpdateCommandDistTest.testFeatureNotEnabled` only asserts the error message and does not assert the expected exit code, and this test file also shows no assertions covering the renumbered `RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE` value. This is a concrete test coverage gap tied to the changes, not a runtime defect by itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: operator/src/test/java/org/keycloak/operator/testsuite/integration/UpgradeTest.java:115 — setEnabledFeatures(List.of(...)) replaces any features the base test deployment already enabled with an immutable list instead of adding to them

adjudication.rationale: In `UpgradeTest.createInitialDeployment`, the diff adds `kc.getSpec().getFeatureSpec().setEnabledFeatures(List.of(Profile.Feature.ROLLING_UPDATES.getKey()));`, which unconditionally replaces whatever list of enabled features might already be present in `FeatureSpec` rather than appending/merging. The use of `List.of(...)` also produces an immutable list (though the diff does not show any later mutation attempts). The claim that the “base test deployment already enabled” other features is not directly shown in the diff, so this is a potential configuration-clobbering concern rather than a proven defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: quarkus/runtime/src/main/java/org/keycloak/quarkus/runtime/cli/command/UpdateCompatibilityCheck.java:46 — Feature gate runs before validateConfig(), so with the feature disabled, invalid or missing options return exit 4 instead of the documented usage error 2, and the docs table only covers exit 4 for `check`, not for `metadata

adjudication.rationale: The diff clearly adds an early feature-gate in both UpdateCompatibilityCheck.run() and UpdateCompatibilityMetadata.run() (check for Profile.Feature.ROLLING_UPDATES) before calling validateConfig(); when the feature is disabled they call picocli.exit(CompatibilityResult.FEATURE_DISABLED) and return. This means argument/option validation is skipped in that case, so missing/invalid options would not surface as Picocli usage errors. However, the diff also adds explicit docs CAUTION blocks saying the commands/operator will fail unless `rolling-updates` is enabled, and tests assert this behavior, so it looks intentional rather than a correctness defect—more a question of desired error precedence/exit-code semantics.

adjudication_records.issue_text: quarkus/tests/integration/src/test/java/org/keycloak/it/cli/dist/UpdateCommandDistTest.java:49 — testFeatureNotEnabled asserts only the error message and never checks exit code FEATURE_DISABLED (4), the new scripting contract documented in update-compatibility.adoc

adjudication.rationale: In `UpdateCommandDistTest.testFeatureNotEnabled` (new at lines ~45-52), the test only asserts the error text and does not assert the process exit code. The diff introduces an explicit exit code contract for this case (`CompatibilityResult.FEATURE_DISABLED = 4`) and the commands call `picocli.exit(CompatibilityResult.FEATURE_DISABLED)` when `rolling-updates` is not enabled. The docs also add an entry for code `4` when the feature is disabled. This is a concrete missing assertion for newly added nontrivial behavior, but it’s not a product defect—just incomplete test coverage.

adjudication_records.issue_text: quarkus/runtime/src/main/java/org/keycloak/quarkus/runtime/cli/command/UpdateCompatibilityCheck.java:46 — The feature-disabled gate on the `check` subcommand has no test; only `metadata` is exercised without the feature

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a feature gate to both `UpdateCompatibilityCheck.run()` and `UpdateCompatibilityMetadata.run()` that exits with `CompatibilityResult.FEATURE_DISABLED` when `Profile.Feature.ROLLING_UPDATES` is not enabled. In `UpdateCommandDistTest`, the new `testFeatureNotEnabled` launches only `{UpdateCompatibility.NAME, UpdateCompatibilityMetadata.NAME}` without `--features=rolling-updates`, so it exercises the metadata path only. adjudication_records.issue_text: operator/src/test/java/org/keycloak/operator/testsuite/integration/UpgradeTest.java:105 — The null (default) update strategy returns early without enabling rolling-updates on the CR, so that case passes only because Dockerfile-custom-image enables the feature at build time; the CR-level enablement the docs require is tested only for Recreate

The finding’s key claim—“the null (default) update strategy returns early without enabling rolling-updates on the CR”—is not visible/verified in this diff, and the only code we can see explicitly enables the feature on the CR. adjudication_records.issue_text: operator/src/test/java/org/keycloak/operator/testsuite/integration/UpgradeTest.java:112 — Docs say the operator will fail when rolling-updates is disabled, but no test covers that failure path or checks that it produces a clear status/error

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds documentation warnings stating the operator/commands will fail if `rolling-updates` is not enabled (docs/guides/operator/advanced-configuration.adoc, docs/guides/server/update-compatibility.adoc). In the operator integration test change (UpgradeTest.createInitialDeployment), the PR explicitly enables the feature via `kc.getSpec().getFeatureSpec().setEnabledFeatures(List.of(Profile.Feature.ROLLING_UPDATES.getKey()));`, so the disabled-feature path is not exercised. The diff does not add any operator-side test asserting what happens (status condition/error) when the feature is omitted/disabled, so the review concern about missing coverage for that documented failure path is grounded, though it’s not a confirmed functional defect in the diff itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: quarkus/tests/integration/src/test/java/org/keycloak/it/cli/dist/UpdateCommandDistTest.java:61 — testMissingOptionOnSave makes only a negative assertion (no "Missing required argument"), so it would also pass if the command failed for any other reason; it should assert exit code 0 or "Metadata:" output

This is a weak assertion: the test would still pass if the command failed for a different reason and produced different error output (or non-zero exit code) as long as that specific text is absent. adjudication_records.issue_text: quarkus/tests/integration/src/test/java/org/keycloak/it/cli/dist/UpdateCommandDistTest.java:44 — The feature is enabled only through the --features CLI flag; enabling it via keycloak.conf/KC_FEATURES env or a prior build is untested, though the operator relies on build-time enablement

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows the new CLI gating requires `Profile.isFeatureEnabled(Profile.Feature.ROLLING_UPDATES)` in both `UpdateCompatibilityCheck` and `UpdateCompatibilityMetadata`, and the dist tests only exercise enabling via the CLI flag (constant `ENABLE_FEATURE = "--features=rolling-updates"`) by appending it to `@Launch` and `distribution.run(...)`. There is no test path covering feature enablement via config/env (e.g., `keycloak.conf`/`KC_FEATURES`) or via prior build-time enablement, even though the diff also adds build-time enablement in `operator/scripts/Dockerfile-custom-image` (`kc.sh build ... --features=rolling-updates`). adjudication_records.issue_text: operator/src/test/java/org/keycloak/operator/testsuite/integration/UpgradeTest.java:115 — setEnabledFeatures(List.of(...)) replaces any features already enabled on the test Keycloak CR instead of appending to them, which could silently change what the base test deployment covers

adjudication.rationale: In UpgradeTest#createInitialDeployment, the diff adds `kc.getSpec().getFeatureSpec().setEnabledFeatures(List.of(Profile.Feature.ROLLING_UPDATES.getKey()));`. This unconditionally replaces the enabled-features list on an existing `FeatureSpec` (when `getFeatureSpec()` is non-null) rather than appending. While this is in test setup (not production code) and may be intended to ensure the preview feature is enabled, it could unintentionally drop any previously-configured enabled features on the test CR and thus alter what the baseline deployment covers.
